applies_why: The judge’s D2 STANDS ground uses the absence of an exhibited verse saying Joseph knew Mary before the birth as a reason for STANDS, which is the kind of verse non-statement ground the rule governs.
quote: no exhibited verse says Joseph knew Mary before the birth.
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.
room: 'a single verse does not state a link or its contrary': one reading limits this to an individual verse's silence; the other treats 'no exhibited verse says' as the same forbidden silence ground. I used the second.
why: Because D2 expressly makes the absence of any exhibited verse saying Joseph knew Mary before the birth part of its STANDS ground, it does what K-S2 forbids.
